---
title: "Private Cloud & On-Premises"
description: "Run PipesHub on your own hardware, including air-gapped networks"
icon: "building"
---

PipesHub is designed to run entirely inside your own network. Nothing about the core product requires an outbound connection once the images are on the host, which makes it suitable for regulated environments and air-gapped networks.

## Requirements

- A Linux host with Docker and Compose 2.20 or later.
- 4 CPU cores and a 16 GB-class machine. The installer stops below 4 cores, and warns below 16 GB of RAM or 20 GB of free disk. Leave more disk for your indexed content. See [System Requirements](/deployment/system-requirements).
- Internal DNS pointing a hostname at the machine.
- A TLS certificate, from your internal certificate authority or a public one.

## Install

The [Deployment Overview](/deployment/overview) covers the standard install. On a machine with internet access:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.pipeshub.com/install | bash
```

## Air-gapped installation

On a host with no internet access, use the `full` deployment type and set `PIPESHUB_OFFLINE=1`. Its image tag, `latest`, has the embedding model built in; the `slim` image downloads the model on first use and cannot do that offline. The `full` type uses Kafka as its message broker.

**On a machine that does have access,** download the deployment files for a release and save the images:

```bash
REF=v1.0.0   # the release you want
mkdir pipeshub && cd pipeshub
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai/$REF/deployment/docker-compose/docker-compose.yml
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai/$REF/deployment/docker-compose/install.sh
chmod +x install.sh

docker pull pipeshubai/pipeshub-ai:latest
docker pull pipeshubai/pipeshub-sandbox:latest
docker pull mongo:8.0.17
docker pull redis:7.4-bookworm
docker pull qdrant/qdrant:v1.15
docker pull neo4j:5.26.0
docker pull confluentinc/cp-zookeeper:7.9.0
docker pull confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.9.0

docker save -o pipeshub-images.tar \
  pipeshubai/pipeshub-ai:latest pipeshubai/pipeshub-sandbox:latest \
  mongo:8.0.17 redis:7.4-bookworm qdrant/qdrant:v1.15 neo4j:5.26.0 \
  confluentinc/cp-zookeeper:7.9.0 confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.9.0
```

These image versions are the ones in the Compose file for that release; check `docker-compose.yml` if you use a different one. If you choose ArangoDB instead of Neo4j, save `arangodb:3.12.4`; for etcd as the key-value store, save `quay.io/coreos/etcd:v3.5.17`.

The sandbox image is only needed if agents should run code. To leave it out, install the `eval` type with the `latest` image (`PIPESHUB_DEPLOY_TYPE=eval ./install.sh --version latest --no-pull`). `eval` uses Redis instead of Kafka, so you can also skip the two Kafka images, but agents cannot run code.

**On the air-gapped host,** copy the `pipeshub` directory and `pipeshub-images.tar` across, then load the images and install without pulling:

```bash
docker load -i pipeshub-images.tar
cd pipeshub
PIPESHUB_DEPLOY_TYPE=full ./install.sh --version latest --no-pull
```

`--no-pull` tells the installer to use the images already present. `--version` must match the tag you saved; otherwise the installer looks for an image you do not have.

After the install, set `PIPESHUB_OFFLINE=1` in `.env` and run `docker compose -p pipeshub-ai up -d`. See [Offline mode](#offline-mode).

## Offline mode

`PIPESHUB_OFFLINE=1` in `.env` makes the existing images run on a network with no route to the internet. There is no separate image, and an empty value (the default) changes nothing. When a container starts with the switch on, it sets each of the variables below for every service, unless you have already set that variable yourself, and logs one line naming what it set and what it kept:

| Variable | Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `TELEMETRY_COLLECTION_FLAG` | `false` | No telemetry is collected or sent, by the Node or the Python services. |
| `HF_HUB_OFFLINE`, `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE`, `HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE` | `1` | Hugging Face libraries read the local cache only. |
| `HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DO_NOT_TRACK` | `1` | Libraries do not report usage. |
| `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP` | `True` | LiteLLM uses its bundled price list instead of fetching one. |

A value you set in `.env` always wins. Values `1`, `true`, `yes` and `on` turn the switch on.

**Already in the image, in every mode:**

- The Docling and table-detector models (see [Models in the image](#models-in-the-image)).
- The OpenAI `cl100k_base` token table used to count tokens, at `/opt/tiktoken` (found through `TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR`), so token counting does not download it.
- The fonts and icons of the dashboard and of the API reference page. They are served by PipesHub itself, not from Google Fonts.

**What you still have to provide:**

- **An embedding model.** Only the `full` image (`latest`) carries one, `BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5`. The `slim` image has no local embedding model and, in offline mode, cannot download one: if the built-in embedding model is selected, the embedding service logs one error saying so and every embedding request fails. Use the `full` image, or configure an embedding service your network can reach.
- **A text-generation model** that the app container can reach, such as a local Ollama or a gateway.
- **The images**, loaded onto the host or into a registry before you disconnect (`docker load`, or a mirror). The installer's pull and the Helm chart's image pulls need that registry.
- **TableFormer `fast`**, if you want it. `PDF_DOCLING_TABLE_MODE=fast` needs weights that the image does not include. A missing `fast` model falls back to `accurate` and logs one warning, online or offline. To use `fast`, build an image with `BUNDLE_TABLEFORMER_FAST=1`.

The switch does not change connectors, hosted model providers or anything else that talks to a service by design: those need the network they talk to.

<Warning>
Check the `pipeshub_hf_cache` volume. It is mounted at `/root/.cache/huggingface` and keeps what it held when it was created. Docker does not refresh it from a newer image. An install that started on `slim` has an empty volume, and that volume hides the embedding model of the `full` image after you switch to it. Either recreate the volume (`docker compose down`, then `docker volume rm <project>_pipeshub_hf_cache`, then bring the stack up again), which also deletes any model you downloaded into it, or place the model you want in the volume yourself.
</Warning>

On Kubernetes, set `offline.enabled: true` in the Helm values. It sets `PIPESHUB_OFFLINE=1` on the app pods and on the parsing pods. See [Kubernetes (Helm)](/deployment/kubernetes#other-settings).

## Models in the image

The images carry the models the PDF parsers use, and load them by path from `/opt/docling-models`. They never download them from the Hugging Face Hub, so they work on a host with no internet:

| Model | Used for |
|---|---|
| Docling layout model (`docling-project/docling-layout-heron`) | Page layout in the Docling PDF pipeline |
| TableFormer `accurate` (`docling-project/docling-models`) | Table structure in the Docling PDF pipeline |
| Heron ONNX layout model (`docling-project/docling-layout-heron-onnx`) | Table and figure detection in the PdfPlumber parser |

- **Where they live.** `/opt/docling-models` is read-only and outside every volume, and the image sets `PIPESHUB_DOCLING_MODELS_DIR=/opt/docling-models`. An older `pipeshub_hf_cache` volume (mounted at `/root/.cache/huggingface`) can no longer hide the models after an upgrade, and Kubernetes needs no volume for them. Do not set `PIPESHUB_DOCLING_MODELS_DIR` or Docling's own `DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH` yourself in `.env` or in Helm values.
- **Image size.** The image grows by about 370 MiB, because the layout and TableFormer weights now ship in it. They used to be downloaded into the `pipeshub_hf_cache` volume at run time, so the total disk use of an install is about the same. An upgraded install keeps its old copy of the ONNX model in that volume. It is harmless and can stay.
- **TableFormer `fast`.** The images bake only `accurate`, the default. `PDF_DOCLING_TABLE_MODE=fast` needs about 145 MB more. Without them the parser logs a warning and uses `accurate`, online or offline. To use `fast`, build your own image with the build argument `BUNDLE_TABLEFORMER_FAST=1` to include them. See [Development](/development) for building images.
- **Other models.** `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` does not affect these models, since they are read by path. Models you choose in the UI, such as an embedding model, still use the Hugging Face cache.

## Choosing models

An air-gapped deployment cannot reach a hosted model provider, so configure local ones:

- **Text generation:** [Ollama](/ai-models/llm/ollama) or [vLLM](/ai-models/llm/vllm) on your own hardware.
- **Embeddings:** [Sentence Transformers](/ai-models/embedding/sentence-transformer), which run inside the PipesHub container. The `latest` image includes the default embedding model.
- **Speech to text:** [Whisper](/ai-models/stt/whisper), which runs locally.

Download the weights for your text-generation models on a connected machine before you move them across.

## Telemetry

PipesHub collects usage telemetry by default. On an isolated network those requests simply fail and nothing breaks, but you can turn the collection off so the attempts stop: switch off **Data collection settings** under **Workspace → General**, or set `TELEMETRY_COLLECTION_FLAG=false` in `.env`. `PIPESHUB_OFFLINE=1` turns it off for you, unless you set the variable yourself.

## Certificates

If you terminate TLS with a certificate from an internal certificate authority, make sure that authority is trusted by the machines people browse from. PipesHub itself does not care which authority signed it.

## Day-two operations

```bash
./install.sh --stop         # stop, keeping data
./install.sh --upgrade      # recreate containers using the current images
./install.sh --uninstall    # stop and delete all data
```

On an air-gapped host, `--upgrade` will not find new images. Load the new images with `docker load` first, then run `./install.sh --upgrade --no-pull`. Before upgrading from 0.x, read [Upgrading to 1.0](/deployment/upgrade-to-1-0).

For backup and restore, see [Backup and Restore](/deployment/backup-restore).
